column1: budget|A plan for how available money will be spent.|Set a monthly budget before signing the tenancy agreement.
income|Money received from work or other sources.|The application asks for your total monthly income.
expense|Money spent for a particular purpose.|Travel is our largest weekly expense.
savings|Money kept rather than spent.|She uses part of her savings to pay for training.
save|To keep money for future use.|We are trying to save for a rental deposit.
spend|To use money to pay for something.|Decide how much you can spend on transport each week.
afford|To have enough money to pay for something.|We cannot afford the larger flat without sharing costs.
account|An arrangement with a bank for holding and using money.|You need an account to receive your wages.
current account|A bank account used for everyday payments.|A current account allows regular bill payments.
savings account|A bank account intended for money kept for the future.|Compare the interest rates before opening a savings account.
account holder|The person who owns or controls a bank account.|Only the account holder can change these details.
statement|A record of transactions on an account.|Download a statement showing your recent payments.
balance|The amount of money remaining in an account.|Check your balance before making the payment.
transaction|A movement of money into or out of an account.|The statement lists the date of each transaction.
payment|Money given to settle a charge or debt.|Payment is due within fourteen days.
cash|Money in the form of notes and coins.|This machine accepts cash only.
coin|A small metal form of money.|You need a coin to use the locker.
banknote|Paper or polymer money issued in a fixed value.|The machine does not accept this banknote.
change|Money returned when someone pays more than the price.|Please check your change before leaving the counter.
cheque|A written instruction for a bank to pay someone.|The office no longer accepts payment by cheque.
debit card|A card that pays directly from a bank account.|You can pay the fee with a debit card.
credit card|A card that allows purchases using borrowed money.|The hotel requires a credit card to secure the booking.
contactless|Allowing payment by holding a card or device near a reader.|Contactless payment is available on local buses.
PIN|A secret number used to authorise access or payment.|Never share your PIN with another person.
ATM|A machine used for withdrawing money or checking an account.|There is an ATM beside the station entrance.
withdrawal|Taking money out of an account.|The bank charges a fee for an overseas withdrawal.
bank deposit|Money paid into a bank account.|Your bank deposit will appear on the statement tomorrow.
bank transfer|Moving money electronically between bank accounts.|Please pay the invoice by bank transfer.
direct debit|An arrangement allowing a business to collect payments from an account.|Set up a direct debit for your electricity bill.
standing order|An instruction to make a regular fixed payment.|A standing order pays our rent on the first each month.
instalment|One of several payments making up a total amount.|The course fee can be paid in three instalments.
invoice|A document requesting payment for supplied goods or services.|The contractor will send an invoice after completing the work.
bill|A statement of money owed for goods or services.|The water bill is due next week.
amount due|The total money that must be paid.|The amount due appears at the bottom of the invoice.
debt|Money that someone owes.|The adviser helped us make a plan to reduce debt.
credit|Money made available to borrow or a positive account entry.|The retailer offers credit for larger purchases.
personal loan|Money borrowed by an individual and repaid over time.|Compare the total cost before taking a personal loan.
lender|A person or organisation that lends money.|The lender must explain the repayment terms.
borrower|Someone who receives money that must be repaid.|The borrower is responsible for monthly repayments.
interest|Money charged for borrowing or paid on savings.|The account pays interest at the end of each month.
interest rate|The percentage used to calculate interest.|Ask whether the interest rate can change.
repayment|Money paid back towards a loan or debt.|The first repayment is due thirty days after approval.
mortgage|A loan used to buy property, secured against that property.|They discussed mortgage options with the bank.
limit|The maximum amount allowed.|Your card has a daily withdrawal limit.
credit check|A review of someone's record of borrowing and repayment.|The provider may carry out a credit check.
security question|A question used to help confirm someone's identity.|Choose a security question that others cannot easily answer.
fraud|Dishonest activity intended to obtain money or another benefit.|Report suspected fraud to your bank immediately.
scam|A dishonest scheme intended to take someone's money or information.|The warning describes a common delivery-text scam.
phishing|A fraudulent message designed to obtain private information.|The training session explains how to recognise phishing emails.
dispute|A disagreement about a charge or obligation.|The bank is investigating the payment dispute.
compensation|Money paid for a loss or inconvenience.|The company offered compensation for the damaged luggage.
claim|A formal request for payment under an agreement.|Keep photographs to support your insurance claim.
coverage|The risks or services included in an insurance arrangement.|Check the coverage before taking equipment overseas.
premium|The amount paid for an insurance policy.|The annual premium is lower if you pay at once.
excess|The amount a policyholder pays towards an insurance claim.|You must pay the excess before the insurer covers the rest.
tax|Money collected by government to fund public services.|The price shown includes the applicable tax.
tax return|A form reporting income and other information for tax purposes.|Keep your records when preparing a tax return.
contribution|Money paid towards a shared fund or cost.|The employer makes a contribution to the pension scheme.
financial assistance|Help with money for essential costs.|Ask student services about financial assistance.
currency|The money used in a country.|Check which currency the booking price uses.
exchange rate|The rate at which one currency is exchanged for another.|The exchange rate may change before your trip.
conversion|Changing money from one currency to another.|The card provider charges a conversion fee.
commission fee|A charge for arranging a financial or sales service.|Ask about the commission fee before exchanging cash.
service charge|An additional charge for providing a service.|A service charge is added to larger group bookings.
late fee|An extra charge for missing a payment deadline.|Pay by Friday to avoid a late fee.
fixed rate|A rate that stays unchanged for an agreed period.|The loan has a fixed rate for the first year.
monthly|Happening or paid once each month.|The membership is paid by monthly instalments.
quarterly|Happening or paid every three months.|Water usage is shown on a quarterly statement.
annual|Happening or paid once each year.|The annual fee is due on your renewal date.
advance payment|Money paid before goods or services are supplied.|The contractor requested an advance payment for materials.
security deposit|Money held to cover possible damage or unpaid charges.|The hire company will return the security deposit after inspection.
quote|An estimated or proposed price for a service.|Get a written quote before agreeing to the repair.
estimate|An approximate calculation of cost or quantity.|The estimate includes materials and labour.
receipt number|A code identifying a particular payment record.|Quote the receipt number when asking about the payment.
account number|A number identifying a particular bank account.|Check the account number before sending the transfer.
joint account|A bank account held by more than one person.|They use a joint account for household bills.
financial advice|Guidance about managing money.|The community service provides free financial advice.
cost of living|The amount needed for everyday essentials.|The survey asks how the cost of living affects residents.
emergency fund|Money kept aside for unexpected essential costs.|We are building an emergency fund for urgent repairs.
value for money|The usefulness or quality received compared with the price.|Compare what each course includes to judge value for money.
expenditure|Money spent on goods and services.|Keep a record of expenditure during the work trip.
arrears|Money that should already have been paid.|Contact the office if your rent falls into arrears.
lump sum|A total amount paid at one time.|You can pay a lump sum instead of monthly instalments.
overdraft|An arrangement allowing spending beyond an account's balance.|Using an overdraft may incur additional charges.
authorisation|Permission for an action or payment.|The bank may request authorisation through its app.
verification|A check that information or identity is correct.|The account cannot be used until verification is complete.
unauthorised|Done without permission.|Contact the bank about any unauthorised transaction.
chargeback|A reversal of a card payment through the card provider.|Ask your provider whether a chargeback is available.
policyholder|The person named as holding an insurance policy.|The policyholder should report changes of address.
liability|Legal responsibility for a cost, loss or damage.|The agreement explains liability for accidental damage.
deduction|An amount subtracted from pay or another total.|Your payslip explains each deduction.
rebate|A partial refund of money already paid.|You may receive a rebate after the account is reviewed.
subsidy|Financial support that reduces the cost of something.|The council offers a subsidy for eligible childcare costs.
eligibility|Whether someone meets the conditions for a service or payment.|The adviser will check your eligibility for support.
means-tested|Based on an assessment of someone's income or resources.|The travel grant is means-tested.
surcharge|An additional charge above the usual price.|There is a surcharge for delivery to remote areas.
audit|A formal examination of financial records or processes.|The organisation keeps receipts for its annual audit.
bookkeeping|Recording the financial transactions of a business.|The evening course teaches basic bookkeeping.
beneficiary|The person intended to receive a payment or benefit.|Confirm the beneficiary name matches the account details.
variable rate|A rate that can change during an agreement.|A variable rate may affect your monthly repayment.
